verdict_A_user_outcome.source_observed: The sidepanel App header mounts one SiteAccessControl for all visible modules. It exposes the temporary Chrome toolbar route, a separately clicked current-origin persistent request, and a separately clicked captured-tab reload. No contains(false) denial gate, timeout inference, auto-request, auto-retry, or auto-reload was added. Existing usePagePrep and SeoView page-key/run guards clear stale output on navigation.
verdict_A_user_outcome.unproven: The new product UI and Chrome prompt have not been observed together in a native build. Existing native proof covers the frozen restricted Prepare failure, temporary activeTab positive control, and an ephemeral DevTools request button only. This source review cannot close the user outcome.
verdict_A_user_outcome.finding: The page identity check before granting/reloading uses the last React-rendered ActiveTabInfo, not a fresh browser tab/document verification. A user who navigates or switches tabs while the popover is open can act before the asynchronous active-tab store publishes the new identity; the control can request the old site's origin or reload the old tab. The contract explicitly requires a live active-page check before reload and safe navigation before grant.

findings.evidence: request() and reload() only compare captured with currentRef.current, set from the rendered tab prop. reloadSiteAccessTarget sends chrome.tabs.reload(captured.tabId) without querying the live active tab or top-frame identity. The hook's refreshActiveTabIdentity awaits tabs.query and webNavigation.getFrame before publishing, leaving a real asynchronous window. The test simulates navigation only by rerendering before the click, so it cannot catch this race.
findings.impact: Wrong-site persistent permission prompt or reload of a tab/page no longer selected; the latter violates the explicit captured-target/live-active identity contract.
findings.remedy: Verify the live active tab, URL, and top-frame document identity at the reload boundary before calling tabs.reload, and make the grant path safe while preserving the direct user-gesture request. Add a test where browser state changes before React receives the new tab prop.

findings.evidence: An in-flight request completion unconditionally calls setStatus based on the captured target and currentRef. Closing/reopening the control resets status but does not invalidate the prior request; a late completion can overwrite the new session's status, including a same-document reopening or a different page's stale banner. No delayed-request/reopen test exists.
findings.impact: The control may tell the person a new access choice succeeded, failed, or is stale based on an earlier choice, which is misleading feedback during recovery.
findings.remedy: Sequence each opened control session and async action; apply a completion only if that session and captured target are still current. Cover late Allow/Deny after close, reopen, and navigation.

verdict_B_engineering_contract.positive_evidence: Grant call is synchronous in the click handler before its first await, scoped to URL origin; no manifest addition. Existing Prepare page-key/run-sequence and SEO audit-run/page-key logic support post-reload fresh work. Existing unit tests cover Allow, Deny, unsupported page/API, rerendered navigation, and a pending Prepare promise followed by reload, fresh result, and ignored late result.
verdict_B_engineering_contract.test_limit: The new connected test renders SiteAccessControl beside PrepareTab, not the App shell or SeoView. Existing seo-navigation-recovery tests cover SEO independently, but there is no connected shared-control plus SEO case promised by the contract. Structural red was a missing-module failure, not a behavior-level red. CI/import and native build verification are separate active lanes; this reviewer did not run a heavy build or browser.
